sourceRequirements: Different transit methods must retain different gravity sensitivity, miscalculation loss, efficiency loss, and proximity tolerance.
Gravitational shear/lensing geometry may be useful terrain for one family and hazardous distortion for another.
Safety sensing must look at least as far ahead as the transit method can place the vessel into danger, subject to imperfect detection and finite margins.
Higher transit maturity must improve not only range but the mathematics, sensing, redundancy, field control, materials, structure, energy efficiency, and emergency recovery that make that range safe.
No safety interlock is perfectly safe; improved technology increases detection and recovery margin rather than eliminating risk.
Mathematical models invented to fill archive gaps remain DERIVED or PROPOSED and must not overwrite confirmed mechanism identity or runtime performance authority.

responseEquation.meaning: The family mathematics evaluates the environment first; the operative technology basis then determines how the required measurement, field actuation, structure, energy delivery, cooling, control, maintenance, signature, and failure behavior are physically realized. Race or manufacturer authority may specialize that basis without changing the confirmed family operator.

basisProfiles.machineryLanguage: Discrete industrial machines, superconductive or field coils, pressure vessels, cryostats, power buses, structural frames, optical/electronic metrology and replaceable modules.

response.fieldActuation: coil/ring/tile/projector arrays with electronically commanded current, field or stress-state control
response.structuralSupport: alloy/composite frames, active mounts and load paths sized for field reaction, recoil, vibration and hull distortion
response.controlBandwidth: distributed electronic/optical feedback with redundant clocks and local controllers
response.sensorLookahead: gravimetry, interferometry, clocks, Q/topology sensors and probes fused into predictive route models
response.energyConditioning: conversion plant -> switchgear/isolation -> buffers -> field buses -> dump/recovery plant
response.thermalRecovery: cryogenic loops, heat stores, radiators, reversible field sinks and emergency dumps
response.maintenanceRecovery: inspection, alignment, insulation testing, coolant service, serialized module replacement and recalibration

basisProfiles.scaleBehavior: Small craft compress functions into integrated modules; capital craft split field formation and control into independently isolated sectors with trunk power/cooling and hierarchical synchronization.

basisProfiles.machineryLanguage: Pressure-balanced wet machinery, ionic/electrochemical power, hydraulic or fluidic actuation, immersed optical control, membrane exchange and wet field surfaces.

response.fieldActuation: pressure-shaped or immersed active surfaces, wet superconductive elements, electroactive membranes and fluid-positioned field elements
response.structuralSupport: pressure cells, compliant wet frames and hydraulically biased supports that preserve field geometry under changing external pressure
response.controlBandwidth: fluidic/electrochemical local control with optical timing where high bandwidth is required
response.sensorLookahead: immersed gravimetric/optical/Q sensors whose calibration includes pressure, density, dissolved gas and refractive-state corrections
response.energyConditioning: ionic/electrochemical sources and converters feeding pressure-balanced storage and isolated high-field interfaces
response.thermalRecovery: bulk working-fluid circulation, phase exchange, membrane heat transfer and emergency pressure/heat sinks
response.maintenanceRecovery: chemistry sampling, flushing, fouling removal, cavitation-margin tests, seal service and pressure cycling

basisProfiles.scaleBehavior: Larger installations gain reservoir and thermal inertia but require sectional pressure isolation and fluid-transit delay compensation; distributed local controllers prevent one long hydraulic loop from setting response time.

basisProfiles.machineryLanguage: Superconductive cryogenic networks, phase-change storage/actuation, photonic timing, contraction-tolerant structure and vacuum-jacketed transfer systems.

response.structuralSupport: contraction-compensating frames, bellows, flexures and cold-aligned supports
response.controlBandwidth: photonic timing with cold electronics and cryofluid actuators
response.sensorLookahead: optical clocks/interferometers isolated from thermal contraction noise and fluid-density drift

response.thermalRecovery: latent-heat buffers, cryofluid circulation, staged heat rejection and protected cooldown/warmup sequences
response.maintenanceRecovery: purity control, seal inspection, contraction alignment, frost/contamination removal and superconductive transition testing

basisProfiles.scaleBehavior: Greater scale improves thermal reserve but multiplies contraction/alignment domains; mature systems divide large field structures into independently referenced cold sectors.

basisProfiles.machineryLanguage: Membranes, tension webs, pressure cells, buoyancy structures, charge-separated flows, electrostatic/ionic actuation and acoustic/fluidic control.

response.structuralSupport: tension webs, pressure boundaries and distributed buoyant load paths rather than rigid terrestrial machinery foundations
response.controlBandwidth: local electrostatic and acoustic/fluidic loops synchronized by distributed timing nodes
response.sensorLookahead: field, gravity and route sensors corrected for density stratification, turbulence, membrane motion and charge environment

transitAssignment.rule: Do not infer an Ar'nock transit family from biological machinery ancestry. A caller-selected family produces a MIXED hypothetical implementation and must preserve that scenario provenance.

validationInvariants: Apply family mathematics before technology-basis embodiment; a basis cannot change a metric drive into a fold drive or vice versa.
The same mathematical safety horizon must produce basis-specific sensor, control, power and recovery machinery rather than identical hardware with renamed nouns.

Every generated improvement must identify whether the limiting gain came from mathematics, field actuation, material science, structure, energy, navigation/sensing, control bandwidth, drive scale/distribution, recovery, or infrastructure.
A higher tier may increase range only when the resolver can point to the changed solvable term and the physical technology that makes that term achievable.
Race-specific overrides require source provenance and may not silently assign an unresolved transit family.
Technology-basis signatures and failures compose with family signatures and failures; neither layer replaces the other.
Safety lookahead and abort authority must remain finite and imperfect even at high maturity.
Numerical coefficients without recovered authority remain PROPOSED calibration values, never setting-wide constants.
